summary_en: Introduces MUnet, a physics-guided unrolled reconstruction framework for photoacoustic imaging that alternates analytic data-consistency updates with supervised neural image refinement. The design keeps the acoustic forward/adjoint operators fixed while learning artifact suppression and detail recovery, and reports improved PSNR/SSIM and runtime over representative MBIR and deep-learning baselines on in vivo sparse-view PAI data.

summary_en: Presents rectified wavenumber-domain beamforming algorithms designed to reproduce conventional delay-and-sum image output while retaining Fourier-domain computational efficiency. The framework covers plane-wave, focused-transmit, and diverging-wave acquisition, achieves SSIM above 0.99 relative to DAS in the reported tests, and reduces computational cost by roughly an order of magnitude, making it directly relevant to fast computational acoustic imaging.

summary_en: Develops a Kirchhoff-Love-plate physics-informed neural network for reconstructing sparse, low-SNR full-optical laser-ultrasonic wavefields and identifying defect-induced scattering. In aluminum-plate experiments the method reconstructs dominant flexural-wave fields using only three signal averages and 20-30% spatial samples, while the accumulated PDE residual provides a label-free defect-sensitive map. This is a particularly direct match to acoustic-optical computational imaging.

summary_en: Uses multimodal deep learning to combine full-field steady-state ultrasonic wavefield measurements with range/depth data for spatially robust material-thickness imaging. Early fusion supplies scene geometry while deformable convolutions compensate for scale and orientation effects; the approach is trained with simulated wavefields and validated on real measurements, outperforming the reported signal-processing baseline.
